sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r2/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row 14 (#13 assets_match_the_task) and Internal Quality Checks row 14; Deterministic Checks rows 4 (check-assets-referenced.py) and 12 (COPY/seed parse)
task/tests/app_context.md, task/tests/test.sh, task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml (all 16 criteria), tests/scored/polish/judge.toml, tests/scored/visual/judge.toml, tests/gates/*/judge.toml
evidence: Paths: instruction.md names /assets/seed_data.json and /instructions; both exist under environment/ (assets/seed_data.json 5701 B; instructions/conversations.md, integration.md, walls-and-retention.md, which cover exactly the topics the brief lists) and environment/Dockerfile (identical to the frozen template) has 'COPY instructions/ /instructions/', 'COPY assets/ /assets/' and chmod -R a+rX on both. task.toml artifacts=['/app','/assets'] so the seed also reaches the separate verifier; test.sh:88 chmods /assets. Solution: solve.sh copies solution/app into /app; solution/app/seed/seed_data.json is byte-identical to environment/assets/seed_data.json (both sha256 f69616e2...be36), matching integration.md 'Copy /assets/seed_data.json into /app'; server.js:29 resolves the seed relative to __dirname with /assets fallback, imports once (settings 'seeded'). No app.db shipped. Seed vs public notes: accounts/names/roles match walls-and-retention.md table and app_context.md; clock 2026-05-12T11:00:00Z matches integration.md; timer_options [null,1,7,30] matches off/1/7/30; M-12 walled=[dev] matches 'Dev Anand is walled from M-12 today'; Gwen owns M-11/M-13, Paul M-12. All parent and read_up_to ids resolve. Seed vs judge assumptions (each recomputed against the clock): K-1 (M-11, 7d, 05-01 09:00, 11d old, not held) expired while K-14 (Harriet reply, 3d19h) and held K-15 survive [deleted_and_expired A]; K-10 at 05-05T11:00:00Z exactly 7d -> gone, K-11 one second later -> shown, and only K-10 contains 'rent review date' [Part B]; K-13 'Probate estimate is 4,200 pounds.' (M-13, 30d, 05-04 09:00, 8d2h, not held, version '2,400') and held K-7 executor -> 7-day change deletes only K-13, no other message contains Probate/2,400/4,200 [timer_changes]; K-17 'Insurer letter acknowledged.' held, 05-03 on 7-day M-11 -> disappears on release [hold_scope]; K-16 'Schedule 2' literal markup, 18h old, survives [safe_formatting]; K-8 'Draft will sent for your review.' 1d21h survives the temporary 7-day M-13 timer [message_links, live_updates]; K-6 'Draft heads of terms ready for comment.' and K-5 'Fenwick' in untimed M-12 [wall_every_route, wall_mentions]; K-3 'Survey booked for Friday.' 3d20h survives; K-2 held, current 'Landlord's notice received and filed.', version 'Landlords notice recieved.' so 'notice recieved' only matches an old version [search_and_transcript]; Dev read_up_to M-13=K-8 leaves K-9 unread before the criterion reads it; polish's held executor mark on M-13 is K-7. Runtime corroboration: raw-evidence-index hashes for golden-run.log (23943bf8...) and functional-before.json (4329fca7...) re-verified; their matching_source_files hashes equal the current frozen solution and seed bytes; scripted golden run (not a configured judge run) reports all seed-dependent checks PASS including persistence (no re-import).
notes: Tried counterexamples: (1) a broken app that ignores the seed timers/holds cannot pass because criteria test seeded expiry, exact-7-day boundary and held survival; (2) a conforming app that treats a seed 'versions' array as earlier versions and marks such messages edited matches the judge; an app that reads the seed from /assets at runtime still works since /assets is a verifier artifact. Seed 'versions' semantics are not documented in a schema, but notes say edited messages show 'edited' and versions, and versions holding the original typo text is the only consistent reading; not a defect. Not independently re-run here: Docker image build from the frozen Dockerfile and the private check-assets-referenced/check-fixtures executables (owned by the deterministic reviewer). The judge criteria depend on earlier criteria's state (persistence relies on prior deletions) - that is a criterion-ordering concern for other rows, not an asset mismatch.
